clusters.state_of_play: Trump reports progress on establishing a permanent US military base in Poland, with a location announcement expected soon. Polish PM Tusk warns that Russia may deliberately or accidentally strike NATO allies, and Western intelligence reportedly indicates Putin is planning a missile strike on a NATO country to test the alliance's resolve, after a Russian attack near western Ukraine forced Poland to close its airspace and scramble fighter jets. Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics has separately warned that Europe is not keeping pace with rapidly evolving drone and aerial warfare in Ukraine, saying most NATO states could not repel a Russian missile attack if the war expands. French President Emmanuel Macron says Russian hybrid attacks against Europe are intensifying and has ordered protection of French infrastructure and defence industry sites, while also calling for an emergency G7 meeting to address soaring energy prices amid the Ukraine and Middle East wars. On the ground, Russia has struck Ukraine's border crossings with Poland and Moldova and its drones are threatening Western officials traveling to Kyiv, even as its eastern offensive appears to be stalling. Separately, Ukraine and Russia are reportedly growing frustrated with US envoy Steve Witkoff and the US-mediated peace process, though Trump is said to see no problem with Witkoff's role. Meanwhile, Russia has begun a three-day parliamentary election - the first since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine - with only parties supporting the war allowed on the ballot; United Russia, which won more than two-thirds of seats in 2021, is expected to retain its dominance amid signs of economic strain among voters, and has used celebrities like NHL star Alex Ovechkin in its campaign. Separately, Latvia has imposed an indefinite entry ban on Ovechkin and sanctioned oligarch Umar Kremlev, a close Putin associate who also has financial ties to Donald Trump Jr. Amid Republican criticism over the propriety of Trump Jr. accepting a lavish Bahamas wedding party from Kremlev, Trump Jr. has repaid Kremlev for the party, and President Trump has publicly defended the arrangement, calling such gifts common.
